site.name: Sherman Bytes
site.description: Deploy an M4-inspired pixel tank onto a live webpage. Breach fortified button bases, build your own cover, and hold the page against escalating squads.
controls: WASD / arrows — drive; mouse — aim the turret
Click / Space — fire; keyboard-only aiming follows the hull
B — cover (2 scrap) · T — pillbox (8) · M — mine (3)
P — pause · G — next hostile base · Esc — Recall
Scoreboard: sound · pause / resume · minimize · Recall
On mobile: joystick to drive, hold Fire; tap Cover, Pillbox or Mine to build

chapters.title: The terrain is the typography.
chapters.body: Letters block tanks and shells. Direct hits clear nearby glyphs into faint binary rubble, opening a crater wider than your tank. Whitespace becomes a route between positions. Explicit data-sherman-wall elements remain solid cover; both movement and shell rays respect their cached rectangles.

chapters.title: Breach the walls. Capture the button.
chapters.body: Four destructible wall segments surround each visible button base. Blast a gap, disable the button, and occupy it for 0.7 seconds to capture it. Friendly bases repair 18 armor per second, fire at nearby enemies, and supply one scrap every 2.5 seconds while occupied. Capturing all factories moves siege reinforcements to the page edges.

chapters.title: A tiny engineer. Your own defensive line.
chapters.body: Aim at clear ground and press B for cover (2 scrap), T for a pillbox (8), or M for a mine (3). A pixel engineer completes one job in 0.65 seconds. Cover and pillboxes sit 52 pixels ahead of the turret; mines deploy 120 pixels ahead to catch approaching tanks. Blocked construction refunds its cost. Pillboxes lead moving targets; mines deal area damage to enemy tanks.

chapters.title: The next wave is already coming.
chapters.body: Siege starts with a four-second preparation window and a ten-tank first wave. Squads arrive in groups of up to three. Later waves introduce more tanks and heavier armor, with at most 40 enemies per wave and 32 alive at once. Clear a wave for eight seconds to fortify, four scrap, and 12 armor. Conquest mode retains the original capture-every-base victory condition.

chapters.title: Salvage makes every shot count.
chapters.body: Start with 16 scrap. Earn supplies from destroyed tanks, breached button walls, base capture, and every four letters you clear. Cannon upgrades still unlock at 20 and 60 XP. Build up to 12 cover segments, four pillboxes, and eight mines. Your own walls stop your shells too, so leave firing lanes or blast a new opening.

chapters.title: Original pixel armor. Shared foundations.
chapters.body: The original M4-inspired silhouette retains its movement, two cached tread frames, independently aiming turret, and recoil. One runtime loop drives tanks, the engineer, construction, and waves. Shells use swept collision segments; movement advances in steps of at most four pixels. A shared TypeScript wave director schedules bounded squads without timers or per-enemy DOM nodes.

site.engine: Shared TypeScript runtime · original single-player tank simulation
site.extra: Shells write literal 0/1 into the existing Text nodes. Optional binaryOpacity styles the real digits using CSS Highlights; without that API they stay fully visible. No replacement letters on canvas, cloned HTML, or per-letter spans. Recall restores still-owned text and button styles.

characters.name: Your Sherman
characters.rules: Drive with arrows or the joystick; hold Fire or Space to shoot. Mouse aiming controls the turret on desktop. Blast text into binary and capture button bases.

characters.name: Scout tank
characters.rules: A lighter enemy that flanks and fires at you. Destroy it for points and two scrap.

characters.name: Heavy tank
characters.rules: Joins siege waves from wave 2. Takes more damage to destroy and drops four scrap. Keep cover between you and incoming shells.

characters.name: Field engineer
characters.rules: B builds cover, T builds a pillbox, M plants a mine. Spend scrap and leave space in front of your tank for construction.

howToPlay.title: Drive and aim
howToPlay.body: WASD or the arrows drive; the mouse aims the turret. Keyboard only, the turret follows the hull. On phones, a joystick drives and a round Fire key shoots.

howToPlay.title: Breach the bases
howToPlay.body: Buttons are bases that spawn tanks. Click or Space fires. Shoot a base down, then sit on it for 0.7 seconds to capture it.

howToPlay.title: Hold what you take
howToPlay.body: Captured bases stop spawning, repair your armor while you occupy them, and defend against nearby tanks.

howToPlay.title: Build
howToPlay.body: B builds cover (2 scrap), T a pillbox (8) and M a mine (3). Aim at clear ground; a blocked job refunds its cost.

howToPlay.title: Survive the waves
howToPlay.body: Siege waves arrive in squads, with an eight-second build break after each wave you clear. Zero armor ends the run.

modes.title: Siege
modes.body: The mode on this page: waves of squads, a build break between them, and reinforcements from the viewport edges once you hold every base.

modes.title: Conquest
modes.body: The original capture-all victory condition. Choose it when you put Sherman Bytes on your own site.

tips.title: Letters are cover
tips.body: Letters block tanks and shells. Blast gaps into faint binary rubble you can drive across.

tips.title: Leave firing lanes
tips.body: Your own cover blocks your shots too.

tips.title: Spend your scrap
tips.body: You start with 16 scrap and earn more from combat, clearing text, captured bases and finished waves.

tips.title: Find the next base
tips.body: G jumps to a hostile base and P pauses. XP upgrades the cannon at 20 and 60.

items.title: Right on 2× and zoomed screens
items.body: On a 1.5× or 2× screen, the tank, enemies, shells and the bases' beacon rings used to draw 1.5–2× too big. Now they sit exactly on the page.

items.title: The scoreboard drags
items.body: Grab the scoreboard anywhere that isn't a key, with mouse or touch. It stays inside the window, also when the window shrinks.

items.title: Readable keys
items.body: The scoreboard's key labels pass WCAG AA contrast in both light and dark themes.

faq.q: Do I need to install anything to play?
faq.a: No. Sherman Bytes plays on this page in your browser. Press Play, and hit Recall when you are done to give the page back.

faq.q: Can I play Sherman Bytes on a phone?
faq.a: Yes. A joystick drives, the round Fire key shoots, and the Cover, Pillbox and Mine keys build.

faq.q: Can I put Sherman Bytes on my own site?
faq.a: Yes. It is open source (MIT). The GitHub repository has the source code, setup instructions and integration examples.

faq.q: What happens to the page when I play?
faq.a: Letters block tanks and shells, and direct hits turn nearby text into faint binary rubble. Recall gives back what the game changed and still owns.
